text:
Recent evidence supports treating diagnostic rankings as hypotheses requiring validation. [Pereira et al., RecSys 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398) distinguish model separability, agreement with full-catalog evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and alignment with true preferences; these are different properties. [Daniil et al., 2024](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/33989/) find evaluation strategy explains substantial disagreement in popularity-bias findings. [Parajuli et al., RecSys 2026](https://mdw.ekstrandom.net/pubs/recsys26-eval) assess validity through agreement between model rankings under conventional evaluation and dense relevance judgments. Full-catalog evaluation removes candidate sampling, but does not eliminate exposure bias or missing relevance labels.

Practical implication for this benchmark: retain the pinned 99-negative HR@10 as the selection objective. Use popularity-stratified or popularity-matched negatives only as auxiliary stress tests; changing the sampler changes the evaluation question. Compare sampled versus full-catalog model ordering with Kendall’s tau or Spearman correlation across checkpoints/configurations. Rank percentiles and positive-versus-negative win rates avoid raw-score scale differences, but measure different behavior from top-10 success. With one held-out positive per user, Recall@10 equals HR@10. Calibrate each proposed diagnostic against observed validation improvements separately by category and on the four-category macro average; no retrieved evidence establishes a universally reliable cheap proxy.

For uncertainty, a suitable adaptation is paired user bootstrap: resample the same users for both models within each category, recompute four category means, then their equal-weight macro difference. Report the improvement and a confidence interval; fixed candidates keep comparisons paired. This interval captures user-sampling uncertainty, not training-seed variability or repeated-search optimism. [Ihemelandu and Ekstrand](https://piret.info/pubs/2023/SIGIR23-InferenceAtScale) support bootstrap/randomization approaches and emphasize effect sizes. Keep the twenty-user qualitative panel exploratory; it cannot establish benchmark gains or unobserved simulator traits.
